title: Prove Settings-denied Skill execution never invokes workspace modules
goal: Add an M8 end-to-end regression proving the Settings-backed execute capability gates Skill execution before any workspace Module is invoked.
context: The read and write capability denial paths now have direct no-module-invocation regressions. This covers the separate execute capability, which must independently deny Skills even when read and write capabilities are enabled.
forbidden_changes: Do not change production execution behavior or grant capabilities.
Do not weaken policy, Agent scope, approval, schema validation, cancellation, workspace path/protected-file checks, secret scanning, size limits, or verification.
Do not treat an unchanged fixture alone as proof that execution was denied.
Do not claim physical-device acceptance from CI.
acceptance_criteria: With Settings read and write enabled but execute disabled, the canonical M8 read Skill is denied.
The denied request emits no moduleInvoked event for any workspace read, write, or search module.
The denied request emits no successful or verified workspace Skill observation.
The fixture remains unchanged and existing positive-path regressions remain unchanged.
Agent Task Contract, M3, and Apple Native Build & Unsigned IPA pass on the final PR head.
verification: Confirm Agent Task Contract, M3, and Apple Native Build & Unsigned IPA pass on the final PR head.
recovery: If the regression exposes a production bypass, investigate the policy boundary rather than weakening assertions. If a required gate fails, repair only within allowed_paths or revert this logical task; never bypass policy or claim device acceptance.
